key_insight: Cortex bridges high-level planning and low-level control with a bidirectionally aligned agent design that turns long-horizon manipulation into executable subtask plans.
engineering_relevance: For robotics and embodied AI systems, the framework offers a practical path to scale long-horizon task execution by standardizing skills, improving data curation, and reducing the semantic gap between planners and controllers.
method: Standardize manipulation into 32 canonical skill primitives with a custom planning interface.
Inject tractability into data generation via representative object attributes and improved trajectory reachability.
Use event-balanced sampling and harness engineering to improve subtask-transition robustness at inference.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports automatic annotation of over 4k hours of open-source video data, 30 hours of simulation data, and gains of 3.1% on Libero-long and 4.1% on RoboTwin, plus zero-shot real-world long-horizon task completion.
watch_item: The approach depends on carefully engineered skill primitives, data pipelines, and task-to-skill constraints, so performance may be sensitive to taxonomy design and deployment-specific harness tuning.
paper_title: Cortex: A Bidirectionally Aligned Embodied Agent Framework for Long-horizon Manipulation
